about: What five Christian traditions and three Jewish movements officially say, and what the Texas and national party platforms say, on eight issues, with sources; and, where a church took a side on specific Texas bills, how each party in the Texas House voted on them. Not yet reviewed by members of the traditions described. CC0.

issues.name: Immigration
issues.description: Who may come to and stay in the United States, and how the law is enforced at the border and within it.

issues.name: Abortion
issues.description: Whether and when the law permits ending a pregnancy.

issues.name: Poverty and welfare
issues.description: Public assistance for people with low incomes.

issues.name: The death penalty
issues.description: Whether the state may execute people convicted of crimes.

issues.name: Guns
issues.description: Who may own firearms and how the law regulates them.

issues.name: Healthcare
issues.description: Who pays for medical care and how people get access to it.

traditions.name: Catholic Church in the United States
traditions.official: Statements approved by the full body of U.S. bishops (USCCB), Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship first. Not staff, committee or diocesan letters.

traditions.name: Southern Baptist Convention
traditions.official: Resolutions adopted by the messengers at an SBC Annual Meeting. Not entity or agency statements.

traditions.name: The United Methodist Church
traditions.official: The Social Principles and the Book of Resolutions, as adopted by the General Conference (2024 revision). The Social Principles are shown in full where they address the issue; otherwise the Book of Resolutions entry on it.

traditions.name: African Methodist Episcopal Church
traditions.official: General Conference resolutions, then statements of the Council of Bishops.

traditions.name: Assemblies of God (USA)
traditions.official: Position papers and official statements of the General Council or its Executive Presbytery. Not columns by its officers.

traditions.name: Reform Judaism
traditions.official: Resolutions adopted by the Union for Reform Judaism (by its General Assembly or North American Board of Trustees) or by the Central Conference of American Rabbis. Not statements by the Religious Action Center's staff, press releases or action alerts.

traditions.name: Conservative Judaism
traditions.official: Resolutions adopted by the Rabbinical Assembly. Not its other statements, and not rulings on Jewish law (teshuvot) by its Committee on Jewish Law and Standards. The United Synagogue of Conservative Judaism publishes no resolutions online.

traditions.name: Orthodox Judaism
traditions.official: Positions adopted by the Orthodox Union's convention delegates or its Board of Directors, as listed in its convention resolutions. The Orthodox Union is the union of Orthodox synagogues, but it does not speak for all of Orthodox Judaism, and Haredi bodies such as Agudath Israel issue no voted resolutions. Not press releases, testimony or letters from its advocacy office.

statements.title: On Immigration, Human Dignity, and the Rule of Law
statements.body: Resolution adopted at the SBC Annual Meeting, Orlando
statements.summary: Calls for enforcing immigration law justly, humanely and with due process, including removing people the government prioritizes for deportation; rejects amnesty without accountability; rejects nativism and ethnic hostility; and asks for particular care for children and families.
statements.excerpt: we reject amnesty, understood as forgiveness of legal violations without accountability

statements.title: Central Conference of American Rabbis Resolution on Immigration & Due Process
statements.body: Adopted by the Central Conference of American Rabbis
statements.summary: Opposes immigration enforcement at or near houses of worship, hospitals and schools except in urgent circumstances, denounces deportations without due process, condemns raids by masked immigration officers, and calls for legislation that balances security with a humane welcome.
statements.excerpt: Denounces deportations without due process procedures

statements.title: Resolution on Opposing Laws Limiting Essential Health Care
statements.body: Adopted by the Rabbinical Assembly
statements.summary: Commits the Rabbinical Assembly to promote everyone's ability to get the medical care they need, condemns efforts to keep pregnant people from health care, and opposes policies that discriminate against LGBTQ+ people or limit access to reproductive health care.
statements.excerpt: promote the ability for all people to access the medical care they may need

statements.title: Special Pastoral Message on Immigration
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops
statements.summary: Opposes the indiscriminate mass deportation of people and calls for meaningful immigration reform, says nations have a responsibility to regulate their borders, and voices concern about detention conditions, immigrants losing legal status, and enforcement near churches, hospitals and schools.
statements.excerpt: We oppose the indiscriminate mass deportation of people.

statements.title: On Standing Against the Moral Evils and Medical Dangers of Chemical Abortion Pills
statements.body: Resolution adopted at the SBC Annual Meeting, Dallas
statements.summary: Calls for revoking FDA approval of mifepristone, laws banning the manufacture, sale and distribution of abortion drugs, enforcing the Comstock Act against mailing abortion pills, and equal protection under the Constitution for the unborn so that all abortion ends, and commits to supporting pregnancy centers, adoption and maternal health care.
statements.excerpt: pray and labor for the abolition of all forms of abortion

statements.title: Social Principles: The Political Community
statements.body: Adopted by the General Conference (2024 revision)
statements.summary: Affirms the dignity and rights of migrants, immigrants and refugees, urges congregations to welcome them, and opposes laws that criminalize or punish people for their migration status, detention in inhumane conditions, the separation of families, and for-profit detention centers.
statements.excerpt: We affirm the dignity, worth and rights of migrants, immigrants and refugees

statements.title: Social Principles, as explained by the church
statements.body: Adopted by the General Conference (2024 revision)
statements.summary: Affirms the sanctity of the life of both the unborn child and the mother, says abortion may be justified in tragic conflicts of life with life, supports the legal availability of medically supervised abortion, and rejects abortion as birth control, for sex selection, and late in pregnancy except in specified cases.
statements.excerpt: tragic conflicts of life with life

statements.title: Social Principles: The Political Community
statements.body: Adopted by the General Conference (2024 revision)
statements.summary: Opposes capital punishment, saying it compounds the loss of life and falls disproportionately on people who are poor, uneducated, from marginalized racial and ethnic communities, or mentally impaired.
statements.excerpt: compels us to oppose capital punishment and the imposition of the death penalty

statements.title: Our Call to End Gun Violence (Book of Resolutions 3428)
statements.body: Adopted by the General Conference (2016, readopted 2024)
statements.summary: Calls on congregations to advocate at the local and national level for laws that prevent or reduce gun violence, and to form partnerships with communities that have experienced it.
statements.excerpt: laws that prevent or reduce gun violence

statements.title: Social Principles: The Economic Community
statements.body: Adopted by the General Conference (2024 revision)
statements.summary: Pledges to work toward eradicating the roots and effects of poverty, rejects teaching that treats wealth as a sign of God's favor and poverty as a sign of disfavor, and endorses policies that guarantee workers fair compensation, sometimes called a living wage.
statements.excerpt: work toward the eradication of the roots and effects of poverty

statements.title: Social Principles: The Natural World
statements.body: Adopted by the General Conference (2024 revision)
statements.summary: Says global warming and climate change already threaten all life on earth and that burning fossil fuels is the greatest single contributor to greenhouse gases, and urges cooperation to end poaching and protect endangered species and their habitats.
statements.excerpt: Global warming and climate change are already creating extreme conditions

statements.title: Social Principles: The Political Community
statements.body: Adopted by the General Conference (2024 revision)
statements.summary: Affirms health care as a basic human right, vows to work toward expanded access to preventive, therapeutic and palliative care, and urges United Methodists to join efforts to create systems that provide comprehensive health protections for all.
statements.excerpt: We affirm health care as a basic human right

statements.title: Social Principles: The Political Community
statements.body: Adopted by the General Conference (2024 revision)
statements.summary: Urges governments to develop systems that emphasize restorative justice, calls for monitoring criminal justice systems for prejudice and bias, and encourages churches to minister to people who are incarcerated and to advocate for criminal justice reform.
statements.excerpt: urge governments to develop systems that emphasize restorative justice

statements.title: Resolution Affirming Our Commitment to Broad, Accessible Reproductive & Sexual Health Care
statements.body: Adopted by the Central Conference of American Rabbis with the Women's Rabbinic Network
statements.summary: Calls on its members and communities to affirm the legal right of a pregnant person to choose to carry or end a pregnancy free from government interference, along with the right to birth control and to comprehensive sex education.
statements.excerpt: legal right of a pregnant person to make their own informed, medically guided choice

statements.title: Resolution Supporting Freedom of Access to Reproductive Health Care
statements.body: Adopted by the Rabbinical Assembly
statements.summary: Supports the Women's Health Protection Act, which would bar government restrictions on abortion services, legislation protecting the transport of birth control and abortion medication across state lines, and the FDA's continued approval of mifepristone.
statements.excerpt: prohibiting governmental restrictions on the provision of, and access to, abortion services

statements.title: A Summary of Standing Policy Positions of the Orthodox Union: Death Penalty
statements.body: Orthodox Union standing policy position, passed by an earlier convention and restated in its 2023 convention resolutions
statements.summary: Supports a moratorium on executions in the United States and a commission to review death penalty procedures.
statements.excerpt: supports efforts to place a moratorium on executions in the United States

statements.title: A Summary of Standing Policy Positions of the Orthodox Union: Gun Regulation
statements.body: Orthodox Union standing policy position, passed by an earlier convention and restated in its 2023 convention resolutions
statements.summary: Endorses gun regulation, including banning certain sophisticated attack weapons, and supports gun control efforts.
statements.excerpt: endorse common sense gun regulation including banning of certain sophisticated attack weapons

statements.title: A Summary of Standing Policy Positions of the Orthodox Union: Energy Policy
statements.body: Orthodox Union standing policy position, passed by an earlier convention and restated in its 2023 convention resolutions
statements.summary: Supports greater energy efficiency and higher federal fuel economy (CAFE) standards, and favors exploring Alaska's oil fields while keeping strict environmental standards.
statements.excerpt: We support an increase of “CAFÉ” standards

statements.title: Introductory Note to Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops
statements.summary: Calls for comprehensive immigration reform that offers a path to citizenship, treats immigrant workers fairly, keeps families together, maintains the integrity of the borders, respects the rule of law, and addresses why people leave their countries.
statements.excerpt: comprehensive immigration reform that offers a path to citizenship, treats immigrant workers fairly

statements.title: Introductory Note to Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops
statements.summary: Calls the threat of abortion the bishops' pre-eminent priority, because it directly attacks the most vulnerable and ends more than a million lives a year in the United States, and pairs protecting children in the womb with solidarity with mothers.
statements.excerpt: The threat of abortion remains our pre-eminent priority

statements.title: Introductory Note to Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops
statements.summary: Lists the death penalty among grave threats to the life and dignity of the human person, alongside euthanasia, gun violence, terrorism and human trafficking.
statements.excerpt: include euthanasia, gun violence, terrorism, the death penalty, and human trafficking

statements.title: Introductory Note to Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops
statements.summary: Supports measures to reduce gun violence, which it lists among grave threats to the life and dignity of the human person.
statements.excerpt: We support common sense measures to reduce gun violence

statements.title: Introductory Note to Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops
statements.summary: Names lack of justice for the poor among the grave concerns Catholics bring to public life, and calls on them to serve the poor and the needy.
statements.excerpt: lack of justice for the poor

statements.title: Introductory Note to Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops
statements.summary: Calls for hearing both the cry of the earth and the cry of the poor, and for responding to climate change with actions that better protect creation for present and future generations.
statements.excerpt: respond to climate change with actions to better protect creation

statements.title: Introductory Note to Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops
statements.summary: Names the need for greater access to healthcare among the concerns Catholics bring to public life, and calls for supporting parents through work, training and help with childcare, healthcare, housing and transportation.
statements.excerpt: the need for greater access to healthcare and education

statements.title: Introductory Note to Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops
statements.summary: Calls for continued reform of the criminal justice system and an end to the use of the death penalty.
statements.excerpt: We continue to seek reform of the criminal justice system

statements.title: Central Conference of American Rabbis Resolution on the Climate Crisis
statements.body: Adopted by the Central Conference of American Rabbis
statements.summary: Commits the conference to advocate, and urges its members to join in advocating, for local, state and federal policies to curb U.S. greenhouse gas emissions and address the harms of climate change.
statements.excerpt: designed to curb American greenhouse gas emissions and address the harms of climate change

statements.title: Central Conference of American Rabbis Resolution on Private Prisons
statements.body: Adopted by the Central Conference of American Rabbis
statements.summary: Supports legislation banning new private prisons and detention centers, and calls on states with private prison contracts to end them as soon as the law allows.
statements.excerpt: Support legislation banning construction or implementation of new private prisons and detention centers

statements.title: Resolution on the Hunger Crisis in America
statements.body: Adopted by the Rabbinical Assembly
statements.summary: Denounces three federal rule changes to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) that it says will weaken food support for people in need, and asks its members to advocate against them and support hunger relief.
statements.excerpt: strongly denounce these changes which will weaken nutritional support for those in need

statements.title: Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops (2015 text, reissued 2019)
statements.summary: Calls for reform that includes a broad legalization program with a path to citizenship, worker protections, family reunification, due process and refuge for people fleeing persecution, and says a nation's right to control its borders should be recognized but pursued justly and humanely.
statements.excerpt: a broad and fair legalization program with a path to citizenship

statements.title: Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops (2015 text, reissued 2019)
statements.summary: Calls abortion the preeminent priority among threats to human life and dignity, because it directly attacks life itself, takes place within the family, and ends so many lives.
statements.excerpt: The threat of abortion remains our preeminent priority because it directly attacks life itself

statements.title: Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops (2015 text, reissued 2019)
statements.summary: Calls for ending the use of the death penalty, saying the nation's continued reliance on it cannot be justified, while noting the Church accepted it in the past for egregious crimes when no alternative was available.
statements.excerpt: our nation’s continued reliance on the death penalty cannot be justified

statements.title: Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops (2015 text, reissued 2019)
statements.summary: Calls for addressing gun violence among the issues that affect human life and dignity.
statements.excerpt: We must work to address gun violence

statements.title: Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops (2015 text, reissued 2019)
statements.summary: Calls for helping families and children overcome poverty through access to education, decent work at fair, living wages and adequate assistance for the vulnerable, and for more development aid, fairer trade and debt relief for the poorest countries.
statements.excerpt: decent work at fair, living wages and adequate assistance for the vulnerable

statements.title: Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops (2015 text, reissued 2019)
statements.summary: Calls for urgently finding ways to care better for creation, especially for the poor, who are most affected by climate change.
statements.excerpt: care better for God’s creation, especially those most impacted by climate change

statements.title: Forming Consciences for Faithful Citizenship
statements.body: Approved by the U.S. bishops (2015 text, reissued 2019)
statements.summary: Calls for providing health care while respecting human life, human dignity and religious freedom, and counts access to health care among the things every person has a right to.
statements.excerpt: Provide health care while respecting human life, human dignity, and religious freedom

statements.title: Statement condemning immigrant family separation
statements.body: Council of Bishops
statements.summary: Opposes the use of Romans 13 to justify separating immigrant children from their parents, supports the ecumenical Faith Leaders Statement on Family Separation, and says a positive resolution is needed for Dreamers.
statements.excerpt: justify and condone the U.S. government's separations of immigrant children from their parents

statements.title: On Gun Violence and Mass Shootings
statements.body: Resolution adopted at the SBC Annual Meeting, Dallas
statements.summary: Calls on governments to examine what drives gun violence and to adopt preventive measures that reduce gun violence and mass shootings in accordance with the Second Amendment, says gun ownership carries great responsibility, and names the human heart as the source of the violence and the gospel as its answer.
statements.excerpt: implement preventative measures that would reduce gun violence and mass shootings

statements.title: Resolution on Health Care
statements.body: Adopted by the Central Conference of American Rabbis
statements.summary: Calls on the President, Congress and the states to preserve and expand access to health care, including keeping Medicare and Medicaid as public programs, expanding Medicaid in every state to people at or below 138% of the poverty level, and barring denial of coverage for pre-existing conditions.
statements.excerpt: preserve and expand access to health care

statements.title: Resolution on Immigration to the United States
statements.body: Adopted by the Rabbinical Assembly
statements.summary: Supports sanctuary cities, a path to citizenship for undocumented residents, the extension of DACA and the closing of immigrant detention centers, and opposes extra funding that would turn immigration agencies into a deportation force and the use of private prisons for undocumented immigrants.
statements.excerpt: allow the eleven million undocumented residents of the United States a path to citizenship

statements.title: CCAR Resolution on Hunger in America
statements.body: Adopted by the Central Conference of American Rabbis
statements.summary: Calls on federal, state and local policymakers to support the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and to protect it from proposals such as turning it into a block grant, and calls on its members to advocate for policies to end hunger.
statements.excerpt: protect SNAP from harmful policy proposals

statements.title: Resolution on American Gun Violence
statements.body: Adopted by the Rabbinical Assembly
statements.summary: Encourages its members to lobby for background checks on all gun sales, bans on military-style assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, and making gun trafficking a federal crime, and urges communities to demand gun violence prevention legislation.
statements.excerpt: required background checks on all public and private gun sales

statements.title: Resolution on Paris United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
statements.body: Adopted by the Rabbinical Assembly
statements.summary: Supports the Clean Power Plan and other energy efficiency measures, urges the U.S. government to pay its share of the Green Climate Fund, and supports a loss and damage mechanism to help developing nations hurt by climate change.
statements.excerpt: support and advocate with other faith-based communities for the Clean Power Plan

statements.title: Resolution on Racial Injustice and Police Brutality
statements.body: Adopted by the Rabbinical Assembly
statements.summary: Calls on legislators to reduce the prison population through community-based policing, changes to sentencing and better programs after release, and calls on rabbis to work with local police to limit the use of force.
statements.excerpt: reducing the historically high levels of our prison population

statements.title: CCAR Resolution on Gun Violence
statements.body: Adopted by the Central Conference of American Rabbis
statements.summary: Urges members of its congregations and communities to demand that Congress enact gun violence prevention legislation, and calls on governments that buy guns to use that buying power to press manufacturers for safer dealer networks and safer gun technology.
statements.excerpt: demand that their Representatives and Senators enact effective gun violence prevention legislation

statements.title: On Global Hunger Relief
statements.body: Resolution adopted at the SBC Annual Meeting, Baltimore
statements.summary: Encourages Southern Baptists and their churches to support the convention's Global Hunger Relief offering through giving and an annual World Hunger Sunday. It addresses church giving rather than public policy.
statements.excerpt: embrace and support the new Global Hunger Relief initiative

statements.title: On the Danger of Age Discrimination in Healthcare Rationing
statements.body: Resolution adopted at the SBC Annual Meeting, Houston
statements.summary: Opposes any public policy that might discriminate against the elderly in their access to quality healthcare, and encourages ministry to senior adults. It does not address health care more broadly.
statements.excerpt: discriminate against the elderly in their access to quality healthcare

statements.title: On America's Growing Prison Population
statements.body: Resolution adopted at the SBC Annual Meeting, Houston
statements.summary: Supports legislation to reduce high incarceration rates without jeopardizing public safety, probation and parole as alternatives to long incarceration for some nonviolent offenders, and programs that help released prisoners reintegrate into society.
statements.excerpt: legislative policies that seek to reduce high incarceration rates without jeopardizing public safety

statements.title: Sanctity of Human Life: Abortion and Reproductive Issues
statements.body: Position paper adopted by the General Presbytery
statements.summary: Holds that human life from conception is to be protected, denies that a legal right to abortion confers a moral right, says historic Christian faith has usually favored the mother's life where childbirth would likely cause her death, and calls on Christians to seek legislative and judicial redress.
statements.excerpt: from conception through death, is therefore to be valued, respected, nurtured, and protected

statements.title: On Global Warming
statements.body: Resolution adopted at the SBC Annual Meeting, San Antonio
statements.summary: Urges Southern Baptists to proceed cautiously in the debate over human-caused global warming, given what it calls conflicting scientific research; urges Congress and the president to support only cost-effective measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and to reject government-mandated reductions; and calls for helping vulnerable communities and for individual and collective efforts to reduce pollution.
statements.excerpt: reject government-mandated reductions in greenhouse gas emissions

statements.title: Official statement on immigration
statements.body: The General Council of the Assemblies of God
statements.summary: Says the borders should be secure so that immigration conforms to the law, supports comprehensive immigration reform reflecting human dignity, compassion and justice, and says ministry to everyone living or working in the country stands apart from questions of jurisdiction.
statements.excerpt: we support comprehensive immigration reform that reflects human dignity, compassion, and justice

statements.title: On Capital Punishment
statements.body: Resolution adopted at the SBC Annual Meeting, Orlando
statements.summary: Supports the fair and equitable use of capital punishment for murder or treasonous acts that result in death, only on clear and overwhelming evidence of guilt, and calls for vigilance, justice and equity in the criminal justice system.
statements.excerpt: support the fair and equitable use of capital punishment by civil magistrates

statements.title: Resolution on Capital Punishment
statements.body: Rabbinical Assembly resolution referred from its 1995 convention. Published by the Death Penalty Information Center, not on the Rabbinical Assembly's own site
statements.summary: Opposes the adoption of death penalty laws and urges their abolition in states that have them, and urges laws that make life imprisonment without parole the punishment for some capital crimes.
statements.excerpt: oppose the adoption of death penalty laws and urge their abolition

statements.title: Capital Punishment
statements.body: Adopted by the Central Conference of American Rabbis at its 90th Annual Convention
statements.summary: Restates the conference's opposition to the death penalty, first stated in 1958 and 1960, says no evidence shows that it deters crime, and opposes it under all circumstances.
statements.excerpt: We oppose capital punishment under all circumstances.

planks.summary: Calls for building state reserves sufficient for Texas to exit the federal Medicaid program, directing budget surpluses to a Texas Health Savings Account until then, and opposing mandates for treatment, vaccination or masks and health insurance surcharges.
planks.excerpt: enabling the state to develop reserves sufficient to exit the federal Medicaid program

planks.summary: Calls for expanding Medicaid, protecting Medicare benefits, making prescription drugs affordable for all, and helping small businesses afford health insurance for their employees.
planks.excerpt: We must expand Medicaid, protect Medicare benefits, and make prescription drugs affordable for all

planks.summary: Calls for more transparency, choice and competition in health care, expanded access to affordable health care and prescription drug options, and protecting Medicare with no cuts.
planks.excerpt: expand access to new Affordable Healthcare and prescription drug options

planks.summary: Calls for protecting and expanding the Affordable Care Act, extending Medicaid-like coverage in states that have not expanded Medicaid, lowering drug prices through more transparency from pharmacy benefit managers, and ending the waiting list for Medicaid home- and community-based services.
planks.excerpt: protect and expand the Affordable Care Act

planks.summary: Calls for basing bail only on a person's danger to society, risk of flight and criminal history, enforcing laws uniformly with punishment that fits the crime, and never using law enforcement to target people for political purposes.
planks.excerpt: ensure bail in Texas is based only on a person’s danger to society

planks.summary: Calls for ending the use of criminal statutes and incarceration to punish problems such as addiction and homelessness, addressing bias in the justice system, and training police to build trust in diverse communities.
planks.excerpt: End the punishment of social problems such as addiction and homelessness

planks.summary: Calls for replenishing police departments, protecting officers from lawsuits it calls frivolous, locking up violent offenders, and cutting federal funding to sanctuary jurisdictions.
planks.excerpt: restore safety in our neighborhoods by replenishing Police Departments

planks.summary: Calls for passing the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, ending state-level use of private prisons, restricting solitary confinement and chokeholds, automatically sealing juvenile records, and supporting rehabilitation and reentry.
planks.excerpt: Democrats will end state-level use of private prisons and detention centers

planks.summary: Calls for abolishing all federal welfare programs, as not an appropriate role for the federal government, and for repealing minimum wage and prevailing wage laws.
planks.excerpt: We support the abolition of all federal welfare programs

planks.summary: Calls for a living wage indexed to inflation for all Texas workers, including tipped workers, and for removing outside work requirements for SNAP benefits.
planks.excerpt: All Texas workers should receive a living wage indexed to inflation

planks.summary: Calls for raising the federal minimum wage to at least $15 an hour and restoring the expanded Child Tax Credit and Earned Income Tax Credit.
planks.excerpt: We'll work to finally raise the federal minimum wage to at least $15-an-hour

planks.summary: Calls for opposing climate change initiatives that obstruct business interests and private property use, including Executive Order 14008, the 30x30 conservation initiative, Net Zero mandates and declarations of a climate emergency.
planks.excerpt: We oppose environmentalism, or “climate change” initiatives

planks.summary: Calls for reducing greenhouse gas emissions through clean energy, alternative fuel vehicles and efficient buildings, rapid decarbonization, and a stronger EPA that sets and meets a net zero carbon emissions goal, and states that climate change is real.
planks.excerpt: Reduce greenhouse gas emissions by supporting policies that develop clean energy resources

planks.summary: Calls for lifting restrictions on oil and gas production, ending the Green New Deal, canceling the electric vehicle mandate and cutting regulations, and pledges to preserve the nation's natural treasures and restore what it calls genuine conservation efforts.
planks.excerpt: We will DRILL, BABY, DRILL and we will become Energy Independent

planks.summary: Calls for continuing the clean energy investments of the Inflation Reduction Act, faster permitting for clean energy, more clean energy on public lands, electrified ports and zero-emissions freight, and lower emissions from buildings and heavy industry.
planks.excerpt: We'll keep pushing to reduce emissions from America's buildings and heavy industry

planks.summary: Calls for capital punishment that is properly applied and reasonably swift, while respecting due process.
planks.excerpt: Properly applied capital punishment is legitimate and should be reasonably swift

planks.summary: Calls for abolishing the death penalty and declaring a moratorium on executions.
planks.excerpt: Abolish the death penalty and declare a moratorium on executions

planks.summary: Calls for repealing or nullifying the National Firearms Act and the Gun Control Act, unrestricted constitutional carry, aligning the Texas Constitution with the Second Amendment's language, and making businesses that bar licensed carriers liable for their safety.
planks.excerpt: Repeal and/or nullify the National Firearms Act of 1934

planks.summary: Calls for preserving Second Amendment rights while adding safeguards against suicide, mass murder, accidents and interpersonal violence, including background checks for gun-show and private sales, and lifting limits on federal research into gun violence.
planks.excerpt: supports the right of law-abiding Americans to own and bear arms

planks.summary: Calls for defending the right to keep and bear arms, as one of the constitutional freedoms in the platform's list of 20 commitments; the platform has no other plank on guns.
planks.excerpt: THE RIGHT TO KEEP AND BEAR ARMS

planks.summary: Calls for universal background checks, a renewed ban on assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, and required safe storage, and cites the administration's red flag laws, narrowing of the "boyfriend loophole" and action on ghost guns.
planks.excerpt: We will once again ban assault weapons and high-capacity magazines

planks.summary: Calls for legislation to abolish abortion by giving the unborn equal protection of the law from fertilization, and for barring public funds for elective abortion and the transport of women across state lines to obtain one, with a private right of action against those who help.
planks.excerpt: We urge lawmakers to enact legislation to abolish abortion

planks.summary: Calls for reinstating the right to an abortion, repealing the Hyde Amendment, protecting IVF, requiring emergency rooms to provide stabilizing care including abortion when medically necessary, and barring penalties on people who travel for an abortion or help them.
planks.excerpt: Expand access to contraception and reinstate the right to an abortion

planks.summary: Calls for opposing late-term abortion, says the 14th Amendment guarantees that no person can be denied life without due process and that the states are free to pass laws protecting that right, and supports mothers, prenatal care, access to birth control and IVF.
planks.excerpt: We will oppose Late Term Abortion

planks.summary: Calls for national legislation to make Roe the law of the land again, repealing the Hyde Amendment, and protecting access to contraception and IVF, and describes the administration's position that federal emergency-care law preempts state abortion bans.
planks.excerpt: we will pass national legislation to make Roe the law of the land again

planks.summary: Calls for securing the border by whatever means necessary, including barriers and a wall, a state Border Protection Unit with authority to repel crossings and deport, faster final rulings and deportation for people in the country illegally, and deportation of non-citizens arrested in violent protests.
planks.excerpt: effectively secure the border through whatever means necessary

planks.summary: Calls for comprehensive immigration reform with an attainable path to citizenship, keeping the Texas DREAM Act and passing a federal one, more family and employment visas, and fewer limits on asylum and Temporary Protected Status, and says being in the country without authorization is a civil offense, not a crime.
planks.excerpt: Enact comprehensive immigration reform, including an attainable path to citizenship

planks.summary: Calls for sealing the border, carrying out what it calls the largest deportation operation in American history, strengthening ICE, raising penalties for illegal entry and visa overstays, and reinstating the Remain in Mexico policy.
planks.excerpt: Republicans will secure the Border, deport Illegal Aliens

planks.summary: Calls for legislation that secures the border, reforms the asylum system, expands legal immigration, keeps families together with a pathway for long-term undocumented residents, and secures the future of the DACA program.
planks.excerpt: secure the border, reform the asylum system, expand legal immigration

JAM 2:16.rv1909: Y alguno de vosotros les dice: Id en paz, calentaos y hartaos; pero no les diereis las cosas que son necesarias para el cuerpo: ¿qué aprovechará?

JAM 2:17.web: Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.
JAM 2:17.rv1909: Así también la fe, si no tuviere obras, es muerta en sí misma.

AMO 5:7.web: You who turn justice to wormwood, and cast down righteousness to the earth!
AMO 5:7.rv1909: Los que convierten en ajenjo el juicio, y dejan en tierra la justicia,

AMO 5:8.web: Seek him who made the Pleiades and Orion, and turns the shadow of death into the morning, and makes the day dark with night; who calls for the waters of the sea, and pours them out on the surface of the earth, Yahweh is his name,
AMO 5:8.rv1909: [Miren] al que hace el Arcturo y el Orión, y las tinieblas vuelve en mañana, y hace oscurecer el día en noche; el que llama á las aguas de la mar, y las derrama sobre la haz de la tierra: Jehová es su nombre:

AMO 5:9.web: who brings sudden destruction on the strong, so that destruction comes on the fortress.
AMO 5:9.rv1909: Que da esfuerzo al despojador sobre el fuerte, y que el despojador venga contra la fortaleza.

AMO 5:10.web: They hate him who reproves in the gate, and they abhor him who speaks blamelessly.
AMO 5:10.rv1909: Ellos aborrecieron en la puerta al reprensor, y al que hablaba lo recto abominaron.

AMO 5:11.web: Therefore, because you trample on the poor and take taxes from him of wheat, you have built houses of cut stone, but you will not dwell in them. You have planted pleasant vineyards, but you shall not drink their wine.
AMO 5:11.rv1909: Por tanto, pues que vejáis al pobre y recibís de él carga de trigo; edificasteis casas de sillares, mas no las habitaréis; plantasteis hermosas viñas, mas no beberéis el vino de ellas.

AMO 5:12.web: For I know how many are your offenses, and how great are your sins— you who afflict the just, who take a bribe, and who turn away the needy in the courts.
AMO 5:12.rv1909: Porque sabido he vuestras muchas rebeliones, y vuestros grandes pecados: que afligen al justo, y reciben cohecho, y á los pobres en la puerta hacen perder su causa.

AMO 5:13.web: Therefore a prudent person keeps silent in such a time, for it is an evil time.
AMO 5:13.rv1909: Por tanto, el prudente en tal tiempo calla, porque el tiempo es malo.

LUK 6:20.web: He lifted up his eyes to his disciples, and said: “Blessed are you who are poor, for God’s Kingdom is yours.
LUK 6:20.rv1909: Y alzando él los ojos á sus discípulos, decía: Bienaventurados [vosotros] los pobres; porque vuestro es el reino de Dios.

MAT 19:23.web: Jesus said to his disciples, “Most certainly I say to you, a rich man will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven with difficulty.
MAT 19:23.rv1909: Entonces Jesús dijo á sus discípulos: De cierto os digo, que un rico difícilmente entrará en el reino de los cielos.

MAT 19:24.web: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
MAT 19:24.rv1909: Mas os digo, que más liviano trabajo es pasar un camello por el ojo de una aguja, que entrar un rico en el reino de Dios.

MAT 19:25.web: When the disciples heard it, they were exceedingly astonished, saying, “Who then can be saved?”
MAT 19:25.rv1909: Mas sus discípulos, oyendo [estas cosas], se espantaron en gran manera, diciendo: ¿Quién pues podrá ser salvo?

MAT 5:42.web: Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.
MAT 5:42.rv1909: Al que te pidiere, dale; y al que quisiere tomar de ti prestado, no se lo rehuses.

MAT 6:11.web: Give us today our daily bread.

GEN 2:2.web: On the seventh day God finished his work which he had done; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.
GEN 2:2.rv1909: Y acabó Dios en el día séptimo su obra que hizo, y reposó el día séptimo de toda su obra que había hecho.

EXO 20:8.web: “Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
EXO 20:8.rv1909: Acordarte has del día del reposo, para santificarlo:

EXO 20:9.web: You shall labor six days, and do all your work,
EXO 20:9.rv1909: Seis días trabajarás, y harás toda tu obra;

EXO 20:10.web: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to Yahweh your God. You shall not do any work in it, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates;
EXO 20:10.rv1909: Mas el séptimo día será reposo para Jehová tu Dios: no hagas [en él] obra alguna, tú, ni tu hijo, ni tu hija, ni tu siervo, ni tu criada ni tu bestia, ni tu extranjero que está dentro de tus puertas:

EXO 20:11.web: for in six days Yahweh made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested the seventh day; therefore Yahweh blessed the Sabbath day, and made it holy.
EXO 20:11.rv1909: Porque en seis días hizo Jehová los cielos y la tierra, la mar y todas las cosas que en ellos hay, y reposó en el séptimo día: por tanto Jehová bendijo el día del reposo y lo santificó.

PSA 24:1.web: A Psalm by David. The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell in it.
PSA 24:1.rv1909: Salmo de David. DE Jehová es la tierra y su plenitud; el mundo, y los que en él habitan.

ISA 45:5.web: I am Yahweh, and there is no one else. Besides me, there is no God. I will strengthen you, though you have not known me,
ISA 45:5.rv1909: Yo Jehová, y ninguno más hay: no hay Dios fuera de mí. Yo te ceñiré, aunque tú no me conociste;

ISA 45:6.web: that they may know from the rising of the sun, and from the west, that there is no one besides me. I am Yahweh, and there is no one else.
ISA 45:6.rv1909: Para que se sepa desde el nacimiento del sol, y desde donde se pone, que no hay más que yo; yo Jehová, y ninguno más que yo:

ISA 45:7.web: I form the light and create darkness. I make peace and create calamity. I am Yahweh, who does all these things.
ISA 45:7.rv1909: Que formo la luz y crío las tinieblas, que hago la paz y crío el mal. Yo Jehová que hago todo esto.

ISA 45:8.web: Rain, you heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness. Let the earth open, that it may produce salvation, and let it cause righteousness to spring up with it. I, Yahweh, have created it.
ISA 45:8.rv1909: Rociad, cielos, de arriba, y las nubes destilen la justicia; ábrase la tierra, y prodúzcanse la salud y la justicia; háganse brotar juntamente. Yo Jehová lo crié.

HEB 4:12.web: For the word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and is able to discern the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
HEB 4:12.rv1909: Porque la palabra de Dios [es] viva y eficaz, y más penetrante que toda espada de dos filos: y que alcanza hasta partir el alma, y aun el espíritu, y las coyunturas y tuétanos, y discierne los pensamientos y las intenciones del corazón.

HEB 4:13.web: There is no creature that is hidden from his sight, but all things are naked and laid open before the eyes of him to whom we must give an account.
HEB 4:13.rv1909: Y no hay cosa criada que no sea manifiesta en su presencia; antes todas las cosas están desnudas y abiertas á los ojos de aquel á quien tenemos que dar cuenta.

PSA 140:12.web: I know that Yahweh will maintain the cause of the afflicted, and justice for the needy.
PSA 140:12.rv1909: Yo sé que hará Jehová el juicio del afligido, el juicio de los menesterosos.

PRO 14:31.web: He who oppresses the poor shows contempt for his Maker, but he who is kind to the needy honors him.
PRO 14:31.rv1909: El que oprime al pobre, afrenta á su Hacedor: mas el que tiene misericordia del pobre, lo honra.

PRO 29:7.web: The righteous care about justice for the poor. The wicked aren’t concerned about knowledge.
PRO 29:7.rv1909: Conoce el justo la causa de los pobres: [mas] el impío no entiende sabiduría.

ISA 25:4.web: For you have been a stronghold to the poor, a stronghold to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat, when the blast of the dreaded ones is like a storm against the wall.
ISA 25:4.rv1909: Porque fuiste fortaleza al pobre, fortaleza al menesteroso en su aflicción, amparo contra el turbión, sombra contra el calor: porque el ímpetu de los violentos es como turbión contra frontispicio.

EZE 22:29.web: The people of the land have used oppression and exercised robbery. Yes, they have troubled the poor and needy, and have oppressed the foreigner wrongfully.
EZE 22:29.rv1909: El pueblo de la tierra usaba de opresión, y cometía robo, y al afligido y menesteroso hacían violencia, y al extranjero oprimían sin derecho.

EZE 22:31.web: Therefore I have poured out my indignation on them. I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath. I have brought their own way on their heads,” says the Lord Yahweh.
EZE 22:31.rv1909: Por tanto derramé sobre ellos mi ira; con el fuego de mi ira los consumí: torné el camino de ellos sobre su cabeza, dice el Señor Jehová.

JOH 14:15.web: If you love me, keep my commandments.
JOH 14:15.rv1909: Si me amáis, guardad mis mandamientos;

GEN 1:29.web: God said, “Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is on the surface of all the earth, and every tree, which bears fruit yielding seed. It will be your food.
GEN 1:29.rv1909: Y dijo Dios: He aquí que os he dado toda hierba que da simiente, que está sobre la haz de toda la tierra; y todo árbol en que hay fruto de árbol que da simiente, seros ha para comer.

GEN 1:30.web: To every animal of the earth, and to every bird of the sky, and to everything that creeps on the earth, in which there is life, I have given every green herb for food;” and it was so.
GEN 1:30.rv1909: Y á toda bestia de la tierra, y á todas las aves de los cielos, y á todo lo que se mueve sobre la tierra, en que hay vida, toda hierba verde [les será] para comer: y fué así.

GEN 1:31.web: God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning, a sixth day.
GEN 1:31.rv1909: Y vió Dios todo lo que había hecho, y he aquí que era bueno en gran manera. Y fué la tarde y la mañana el día sexto.

MAT 6:26.web: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
MAT 6:26.rv1909: Mirad las aves del cielo, que no siembran, ni siegan, ni allegan en alfolíes; y vuestro Padre celestial las alimenta. ¿No sois vosotros mucho mejores que ellas?

MAT 6:27.web: “Which of you by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?
MAT 6:27.rv1909: Mas ¿quién de vosotros podrá, congojándose, añadir á su estatura un codo?

MAT 6:28.web: Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,
MAT 6:28.rv1909: Y por el vestido ¿por qué os congojáis? Reparad los lirios del campo, cómo crecen; no trabajan ni hilan;

MAT 6:29.web: yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.
MAT 6:29.rv1909: Mas os digo, que ni aun Salomón con toda su gloria fué vestido así como uno de ellos.

MAT 6:30.web: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?
MAT 6:30.rv1909: Y si la hierba del campo que hoy es, y mañana es echada en el horno, Dios [la] viste así, ¿no [hará] mucho más á vosotros, [hombres] de poca fe?

ROM 8:22.web: For we know that the whole creation groans and travails in pain together until now.
ROM 8:22.rv1909: Porque sabemos que todas las criaturas gimen á una, y á una están de parto hasta ahora.

ROM 8:23.web: Not only so, but ourselves also, who have the first fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for adoption, the redemption of our body.
ROM 8:23.rv1909: Y no sólo ellas, mas también nosotros mismos, que tenemos las primicias del Espíritu, nosotros también gemimos dentro de nosotros mismos, esperando la adopción, [es á saber], la redención de nuestro cuerpo.

ROM 8:24.web: For we were saved in hope, but hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for that which he sees?
ROM 8:24.rv1909: Porque en esperanza somos salvos; mas la esperanza que se ve, no es esperanza; porque lo que alguno ve, ¿á qué esperarlo?

GEN 1:4.web: God saw the light, and saw that it was good. God divided the light from the darkness.
GEN 1:4.rv1909: Y vió Dios que la luz era buena: y apartó Dios la luz de las tinieblas.

GEN 1:10.web: God called the dry land “earth”, and the gathering together of the waters he called “seas”. God saw that it was good.
GEN 1:10.rv1909: Y llamó Dios á la seca Tierra, y á la reunión de las aguas llamó Mares: y vió Dios que era bueno.

GEN 1:12.web: The earth yielded grass, herbs yielding seed after their kind, and trees bearing fruit, with their seeds in it, after their kind; and God saw that it was good.
GEN 1:12.rv1909: Y produjo la tierra hierba verde, hierba que da simiente según su naturaleza, y árbol que da fruto, cuya simiente está en él, según su género: y vió Dios que era bueno.

GEN 1:18.web: and to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness. God saw that it was good.
GEN 1:18.rv1909: Y para señorear en el día y en la noche, y para apartar la luz y las tinieblas: y vió Dios que era bueno.

GEN 2:15.web: Yahweh God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
GEN 2:15.rv1909: Tomó, pues, Jehová Dios al hombre, y le puso en el huerto de Edén, para que lo labrara y lo guardase.

ISA 11:6.web: The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat, the calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf together; and a little child will lead them.
ISA 11:6.rv1909: Morará el lobo con el cordero, y el tigre con el cabrito se acostará: el becerro y el león y la bestia doméstica andarán juntos, y un niño los pastoreará.

LEV 19:32.web: “‘You shall rise up before the gray head and honor the face of the elderly; and you shall fear your God. I am Yahweh.
LEV 19:32.rv1909: Delante de las canas te levantarás, y honrarás el rostro del anciano, y de tu Dios tendrás temor: Yo Jehová.

PRO 16:31.web: Gray hair is a crown of glory. It is attained by a life of righteousness.
PRO 16:31.rv1909: Corona de honra es la vejez, que se hallará en el camino de justicia.

MAT 18:15.web: “If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.
MAT 18:15.rv1909: Por tanto, si tu hermano pecare contra ti, ve, y redargúyele entre ti y él solo: si te oyere, has ganado á tu hermano.

MAT 18:16.web: But if he doesn’t listen, take one or two more with you, that at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.
MAT 18:16.rv1909: Mas si no [te] oyere, toma aún contigo uno ó dos, para que en boca de dos ó de tres testigos conste toda palabra.

MAT 18:17.web: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the assembly. If he refuses to hear the assembly also, let him be to you as a Gentile or a tax collector.
MAT 18:17.rv1909: Y si no oyere á ellos, dilo á la iglesia: y si no oyere á la iglesia, tenle por étnico y publicano.

MAT 18:18.web: Most certainly I tell you, whatever things you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever things you release on earth will have been released in heaven.
MAT 18:18.rv1909: De cierto os digo [que] todo lo que ligareis en la tierra, será ligado en el cielo; y todo lo que desatareis en la tierra, será desatado en el cielo.

MAT 18:19.web: Again, assuredly I tell you, that if two of you will agree on earth concerning anything that they will ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven.
MAT 18:19.rv1909: Otra vez os digo, que si dos de vosotros se convinieren en la tierra, de toda cosa que pidieren, les será hecho por mi Padre que está en los cielos.

MAT 18:20.web: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”
MAT 18:20.rv1909: Porque donde están dos ó tres congregados en mi nombre, allí estoy en medio de ellos.
